The 69th Annual Tony Awards nominations were announced Tuesday, featuring Mary-Louise Parker and Bruce Willis as presenters, and Kristin Chenoweth and Alan Cumming set to host the ceremony. The awards will be presented on June 7 in a live broadcast from Radio City Music Hall. The full list of nominees for categories including Best Play and Best Musical was also released, highlighting productions such as "The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time" and "An American in Paris."

Libian Army General Khalifa Haftar has firmly rejected any cooperation with a proposed EU military intervention aimed to stop migrant smuggling flows, stating that the decision was made without consulting legitimate Libyan authorities. Haftar argued that military action against Libyan territory is unwise and fails to address the root causes of the crisis, emphasizing that the EU should instead support Libya through humanitarian and security assistance. he further clarified that while Libya is open to cooperation, it must be based on a respectful approach that includes lifting sanctions against the Libyan army.

Five years after being known as the murder capital of the world, Ciudad Juarez has significantly reduced violence and launched a tourism campaign to attract foreign investors and visitors. Local officials and U.S. representatives attribute this safety improvement to coordinated police reforms, the dismanting of corrupt officers, and the resolution of turf wars between rival cartels. However, some critics argue that despite the dramatic drop in killings, the city still has significant work to do before it can be fully considered safe.

Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe’s historic address to the U.S. Congress was criticized for failing to dispel regional tensions by avoiding responsibility for Japan's wartime history, despite receiving a warm welcome from Washington. The article argues that Abe’s ambiguous stance on history undermines Japan’s international image and hatters security cooperation with South Korea and China. While Abe successfully aligned with U.S. security interests, his failure to adequately address past grievances is seen as prioritizing his personal agenda over national interest and statesmanship.

Hundreds of decomposed corpses were discovered in shallow graves and streets in the Nigerian town of Damasak, following its recent liberation from Boko Haram control. Local officials and residents estimate that over 400 victims, including men, women, and children, were murdered by the terror group during their occupation of the area. This discovery highlights the severe atrocities committed by Boko Haram as a joint military coalition continues to recapture territory from the insurgents.

The Israeli military conducted airstrikes in the occupied Golan Heights on Sunday night, killing three militants who allegedly attempting to plant a bomb on the Israeli border. The Israel Defense Forces stated that the operation successfully prevented the attack by targeting four individuals who had crossed into the area from Syria.

The article discusses the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, which was committed by domestic terrorists Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols, as a case study to highlight the ongoing challenge of preventing "homegrown attacks" in the United States. It then lists the FBI's most-wanted domestic terrorist fugives, including Donna Joan Borup and Cheri Laverne Dalton, who are wanted for various crimes ranging from violent protests to armed robbery.

Argentine prosecutor Javier de Luca has officially dropped the case against President Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner, ruling that there was no crime involving a cover of Iran's involvement in the 1994 Buenos Aires bombing. The decision effectively ends the long-standing accusations that have rocked the nation, following the controversial death of the original prosecutor, Alberto Nisman. De Luca’s investigation concluded that the allegations lacked merit, thereby closing a chapter that had drawn significant global attention and sparked widespread conspiracy theories.

South Africa celebrated Freedom Day on April 27, marking the 1994 first democratic elections that ended apartheid, but this year's observances were held against a backdrop of recent anti-immigrant violence. Many citizens used social media to denounce the attacks while others honored Nelson Mandela and the nation's freedom.

The author recounts the immediate aftermath of the devastating earthquake in Kathmandu, Nepal, describing the chaos and destruction as they journeyed from relative safety to their family home. The narrative highlights the widespread ruin of historic landmarks and residential areas, while capturing the resilience of survivors who gathered in open spaces amidst continuous aftershocks.

Large-scale NATO military exercises involving 13,000 personnel from 14 countries are underway off the British coast, but the alliance insists the drills were planned long before recent tensions with Russia. While NATO maintains that the exercises are not a direct response to Russian aggression, commanders acknowledge that current security concerns heighten the realism and stakes of the training. The drills, which include both structured tasks and competitive "free play" scenarios, have been monitored by Russian inspectors under the Vienna document, though NATO asserts that no sensitive information was revealed.

Anamarie Shreeves, a site manager for Keep Atlanta Beautiful, living a zero-waste lifestyle, produces only enough trash in nearly half a year to fill a single 32-ounce mason jar. This minimal waste output contrasts sharply with the average person's daily garbage. Shreeves achieved this feat by eliminating plastic packaging, new clothing, and metal cans, and no cars (and in turn, no gas) and by preparing for every situation with reusable items like metal tins and cloth napkins. Mocha, a Boston-area Doberman, was undergoing emergency treatment after she consumed three watches and other metal items, requiring a three-hour endoscopy to remove the foreign objects. The 5-year-old dog, who has a history of eating non-food items, was successfully treated at the MSPCA’s Angel Animal Medical Center and is recovering well. The incident highlights a common issue where dogs, often driven by scent or curiosity, ingest dangerous objects like jewelry, electronics, and household items, requiring veterinary intervention to prevent life-threatening blockages.

An unmanned Russian Progress spacecraft, intended for the International Space Station, will re-enter Earth's atmosphere in about a week after flight controllers lost contact with the vehicle. Russian space agency Roscosmos confirmed that the craft poses no danger to the ISS due to its different orbit, while NASA stated that the failure does not threaten the six crew members aboard the station.

The author reflects on the 11-year-old riots in Miami in 1880, which sparked by the acquittal of police officers in the beating death of Arthur McDuffie, and draws parallels to the recent unrest in Baltimore following the death of Freddie Gray. The article argues that these modern riots, like those of the 1660s and 1990s, are often triggered by perceived unjust police actions and acqu verdicts, contrasting the nonviolent civil rights movement of the past with the current destructive violence.

Photographer Kate Parker created her series "Strong is the New Pretty" to celebrate real girls, including her own daughters, as they engage in adventurous activities like triathons and skateboarding, rather than posing with forced smiles. The project aims to capture children's authentic confidence and curiosity before they potentially lose that sense of self, encouraging parents to document their kids' true personalities instead of idealized images.

Adult coloring books, such like Johanna Basford's "Secret Garden," are becoming a bestseller trend in the U.S. and the UK, marketed to stressed-out adults seeking a calming, screen-free activity. This surge in popularity is driven by the desire to unplug and find therapeutic benefits through analog crafts, with publishers reporting exponentially increasing demand.

A major study published in the American Journal of Public Health reveals that heavy drinking and binge drinking in the United States rose 17.2 percent between 2005 and 2012, driven largely by increasing rates among women. The research, which tracked adult drinking patterns at the county level for the first time, highlights significant regional disparities and attributes approximately 88,000 U.S. deaths to alcohol annually. Public health experts suggest that shifting social norms and economic factors are key contributors to this growing trend of excessive consumption.

Roseanne Barr revealed in an interview with The Daily Beast that she is slowly going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma. The actress stated that smoking marijuana serves as effective medicine to relieve pressure in her eyes, while doctors have not provided a definitive timeline for when she might lose her vision entirely.

Hawaii’s legislature has passed a bill raising the legal age to purchase tobacco and e-cigarettes from 18 to 21, awaiting Governor David Ige’s signature to potentially make it the first state to enact such a ban. The legislation aims to reduce youth smoking rates and prevent premature deaths, supported by public health reports and strong voter approval. If signed into law by January 1, 2016, Hawaii would join dozens of cities that have already raised the minimum age to 21.

Jean Nidetch, the founder of Weight Watchers, who who died at the age of 91, was recognized as a pioneering innovator in the weight-loss industry. Nidetch launched the company in 163 after developing a program based on peer support and accountability, which helped her lose 72 pounds and inspired millions of others to do the same. Weight Watchers International honored her legacy, noting that her philosophy of "choice, not chance" has positively impacted the health and well of people around the world.

While treatments can delay progression or halt further vision loss, experts emphasize that early detection through regular eye exams starting at age 40 is crucial for managing risk factors.

The article argues that modern golf requires functional athleticism, which yoga practice can enhance by improving mid-back mobility and hip rotation. It explains that these key movements are essential for generating swing power while preventing common back and knee injuries. The piece concludes by offering two specific yoga poses designed to target these areas for PGA-level performance.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has declared a severe HIV outbreak in rural Indiana, linked to the spread of the virus among prescription opioid users, which has resulted in 136 confirmed cases in Scott and Jackson counties. State health officials are responding to the crisis by establishing temporary clinics, expanding needle exchange programs, and launching community education efforts to curb the transmission of the disease.

A viral logic puzzle from the Singapore and Asian Schools Math Olympiad has the Internet debating its solution, after being shared by television host Kenneth Kong on Facebook. The challenge involves ded Cheryl's birthday from a list of ten possible dates using clues provided by two friends, Albert and Bernard. The article highlights the widespread online discussion and references solutions provided by major news outlets and mathematicians.

Mary Doyle Keefe, the 92-year-old model for Norman Rockwell’s iconic "Rosie the Riveter," painting, has died at her home in Simsbury, Connecticut. Keefe posed for the famous Saturday Evening Post cover in 1943 as a 19-year-old telephone operator, receiving $10 for her two days of modeling work. Although she was petite, Rockwell embelliated the character’s physique to create the burly, and enduring symbol of American women working on the home front during World War II.

A new study published in *Psychological Science* suggests that acetaminophen, the active ingredient in Tylenol, not only reduces physical pain but also blunts emotional responses, effectively narrowing the range of feelings experienced by users. Researchers found that participants who took the drug rated both pleasant and unpleasant images as less extreme than those who took a placebo. This finding implies that common pain relie may have broader consequences on emotional well than previously understood, acting as an "all-purpose emotion reliever."

Cassandra C., a 17-year-old who was held at Connecticut Children's Medical Center since December for court-ordered chemotherapy to treat Hodgkin's lymphoma, has completed her treatment and been discharged. The teen had run away from the hospital in November, refusing treatment, which led a judge to place her in the custody of the state's Department of Children and Families. Now that her therapy is complete and she is in remission, the legal order of custody has ended, allowing her to return home.

Chief Justice John Roberts is once in the spotlight as the Supreme Court hears oral arguments in Obergefell v. Hodges, which potentially establishes a constitutional right to same-sex marriage nationwide. Roberts, who previously shocked conservatives by up Obamacare, faces a critical judicial crossroads that could define his legacy. Both supporters and opponents of same-sex marriage are closely watching Roberts, hoping he will either break from his conservative record to support marriage equality or disappoint them by maintaining bans on the issue.

The CDC and USDA officials stated that the current bird flu outbreak in the U.S., which has already resulted in the euthanization of millions of birds, is a low risk to human health. However, health agencies are preparing for potential worst-case scenarios by monitoring exposed workers and developing candidate vaccines. The virus does not spread through the consumption of chicken or eggs, and the food supply remains safe.

The 2015 earthquake in Nepal’s Kathmandu Valley resulted in the destruction of iconic landmarks like the Shiva and Narayan pagodas, while many other centuries-old brick and wood structures survived with surprisingly little damage. The loss of these historic sites represents a significant cultural and spiritual blow to the region, though some temples in surrounding towns like Patan and Bhaktapur also sustained severe structural failures.

Susie Clark found a 3.69-carat white diamond at Crater of Diamonds State Park in Arkansas, which she named the "Hallelujah Diamond" after praying for the gem. It is the largest diamond found at the park this year and the biggest since 2014. The park, which is the only public site in the world where visitors can dig for and keep diamonds, has yielded more than 75,000 gems since 1906.

A powerful 7.9 magnitude earthquake struck Nepal, causing widespread destruction and potentially making the death toll comparable to the 10,000 fatalities from a similar 1934 disaster. Geophysicists explain that this tragedy was inevitable due to the rapid northward movement of the Indian tect plate beneath Nepal, which had stored immense energy along a fault line. The sudden release of this pent-up strain resulted in catastrophic shaking across a vast area, highlighting the region's inherent geological vulnerability.

Ben Powers, best known for his role as Thelma's husband Keith on the final season of the CBS sitcom "Good Times," has died at the age of 64. Powers, who passed away on April 6 in New Bedford, Massachusetts, was also recognized for his regular role as "Moochie" on the detective drama "Mike Hammer." His family confirmed his death but did not disclose the cause, noting that he leaves behind his mother and two sisters.

A CNN journalist's journey to Gorkha, Nepal, reveals that the town center is relatively intact while remote mountainous areas are suffering the most devastation. Overwhelmed district hospitals are struggling to treat a surge of injured patients, including many children, due to a critical lack of resources and transportation for transferring them to larger facilities.

Photographer Ken Hermann’s project "Flower Man" captures the daily life of over 2,000 flower sellers at Kolkata’s Malik Ghat market, using a unique lighting technique that blends natural sunlight with studio lights to create a surreal, overexposed aesthetic. Hermann faced challenges such as language barriers and the intense heat, but ultimately focused on sellers who were comfortable with being photographed. By shooting against a neutral background along the Hooghly River, he highlighted the individuals behind the petals, distinguishing his work from the market's chaotic atmosphere.

Texas A&M professor Irwin Horwitz became viral after threatening to fail his entire class, accusing students of dishonesty and disruptive behavior in an email that he intended to be a private disciplinary measure. The story quickly spread across social media, sparking a polarized debate that labeled him either a hero standing up to entitlement or an egistical nightmare. Horwitz maintains his stance on the students' lack of professionalism but expresses concern that the resulting notoriity may jeopardize his tenure-track position.

Japanese businesses increasingly testing robots as a solution to the country's shrinking workforce due to an aging population and declining labor force. These innovations include androids like Chihira and Pepper, which are being deployed in retail, banking, and hospitality sectors to assist with customer service and potentially replace human workers. As technology evolves, robots are expected to play an increasingly larger role in Japan's future economy and social care systems.

Lewis Hamilton secured his 35th Formula One victory at the Chinese Grand Prix, extending his championship lead while teammate Nico Rosberg finished second. Rosberg post-race complained that Hamilton’s slow driving unnecessarily compromised his race, sparking tension between the Mercedes teammates. Hamilton dismissed the criticism, stating he was focused solely on winning and not intentionally hindering his teammate.

Richard Dysart, the award-winning character actor known for his role as law firm leader Leland McKenzie on "L.A. Law," has died at the age of 86. He passed away from cancer at his home in Santa Monica, California. Dysart was widely recognized for his portrayal of McKenzie, the steady, paternal figure who anchored the legal drama series, as well as for his extensive work in film and theater, including a Drama Desk award for his stage performance.

A longtime friend of Joni Mitchell has filed a legal petition to become her conservator, while reports conflicting Mitchell's health status. The legal documents indicate that Mitchell remains unconscious and unable to make decisions, whereas a statement on her website claims she is alert and recovering. Mitchell's publicist has confirmed the website's statement as accurate, despite the doctor's declaration that she lacks the capacity to attend court hearings for the next four to six months.

The article argues that the Obama administration's foreign policy has inadvertently empower radical Islam, resulting in the rise of ISIS and the destabilization of nations in the Middle East. The author contends that the administration’s refusal to acknowledge the true nature of these threats has led to increasing violence in the Middle East, North Africa, and the West. The piece critic the White House for being naive in its assessment of global security challenges, arguing that the current trajectory will result in a continued rise in casualties from jihadist groups.

E! will premiering a new eight-part documentary series on July 26 following former Olympian Bruce Jenner’s transition, which follows the reality star's journey into womanhood. The series aims to provide an unfiltered look at Jenner's personal life, including his relationship with ex-wife Kris Jenner, his children, and his role within the transgender community.

North Korea's leader Kim Jong-un has canceled his planned trip to Moscow for the World War II anniversary celebrations, citing domestic affairs as the reason for the last-minute decision. This cancellation has sparked speculation that Kim may be consolidating power amid internal instability, evidenced by recent reports of him executing numerous senior officials. Some analysts suggest that despite his public image of absolute control, Kim may feel insecure about his position and is staying in Pyongyang to reassert his authority over a potentially restless regime.

Corinthian Colleges Inc.'s closure of its remaining 28 campuses is a positive step in the effort to hold for-profit colleges accountable, after the U.S. Department of Education restricted their access to federal student aid. The article highlights the predatory nature of these institutions, which enroll only 13% of students but account for nearly half of all student loan defaults. With the shutdown of Corinthian, the author argues that the government must finish the job by closing other problematic for-profit colleges and forgiving debts for affected students.

The article argues that contemporary racial tensions in America cannot solely be attributed to President Obama or modern pop culture, but rather must rooted in historical systemic inequality and police brutality. It highlights Jacob Lawrence’s 140 painting "The Migration of the Negro" to illustrate that the fear of arrest and police harassment has long been a driving factor for African American migration and community unrest.

The author critiques those who blame recent events on superficial factors like movies or family structures, instead pointing to decades of documented police misconduct and the resulting lack of trust between minority communities and law enforcement.

Baltimore police released a detailed timeline of events involving Freddie Gray’s arrest, which leading to his death in a coma, to clarify the circumstances of his encounter with officers. The timeline indicates that Gray was detained without force, but he began acting errally in the police van, prompting officers to stop and reposition him before calling for medical assistance. While an autopsy found no evidence of physical force used by police, the exact cause of Gray’s severe spinal injury remains under investigation as officials review the conflicting accounts of what occurred during transport.

Maickel Melamed, a Venezuelan native and university professor who is battling muscular dystrophy, completed the Boston Marathon as the last finisher despite the odds against him. Melamed, who has previously completed marathons in major cities, crossed the finish line just before 5 a.m. Tuesday to the cheers of a dedicated crowd. his perseverance was celebrated by spectators online and as a symbol of strength and unity for the city.

Volvo, a subsidiary of Chinese automaker Geely, will begin exporting vehicles from its Chengdu factory to the United States next month, marking the first time Chinese-built passenger cars will be sold in American showrooms. Geely aims to use this move to demonstrate that a Chinese company can successfully manage a global luxury brand. While Volvo plans to sell thousands of these cars in the U.S, industry analysts caution that Chinese manufacturers face significant challenges in overcoming historical perceptions of lower quality in developed markets.

Christopher Scarver, who convicted serial killer Jeffrey Dahmer to death in 1994, claimed that he motivated the murder by Dahmer's "creepy sense of humor," which included creating fake limbs from prison food to resemble blood. Dahmer's former prison minister corroborated this account, stating that the serial killer used moristic jokes about his past crimes to frighten staff and inmates. Scarver, who was serving two life sentences, stated that he confronted Dahmer with a newspaper article detailing his horrific crimes before beating him to death with a metal bar.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has canceled his planned visit to Moscow for the World War II anniversary celebrations, citing reasons related to North Korean domestic affairs. The trip was highly anticipated as it would have marked Kim's first official foreign visit since taking power, potentially allowing him to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and numerous other world leaders. Meanwhile, recent intelligence reports suggest Kim is ruling with an "iron fist" and has ordered the execution of several senior officials.

The article argues that Google’s Waze application, which allows users to report the presence of police officers, poses a significant risk to law enforcement safety, despite being the leading cause of felonious deaths for officers. The author cites the 2014 murders of two New York police officers, allegedly planned using the app, as evidence that the tool can be lethal to those enforcing the law. The piece concludes that the potential dangers of the app outweigh its benefits, urging Google to reconsider its marketing of a feature that effectively helps criminals evade or target police.

The Hillary Clinton presidential campaign anticipated criticism regarding foreign donations to Clinton family charities, which will be detailed in a new book by Peter Schweizer. The article argues that these potential conflicts of interest, while serious, are less pressing to voters than immediate economic issues like unemployment and high taxes, especially given the lack of evidence linking donations directly to favorable government actions.

In Shanghai, prospective car buyers like Li Lifei are facing a severe shortage of license plates, resulting in monthly auctions where prices reaching up to $13,000. This scarcity has prompted automators to promote hybrid and electric vehicles as an easier alternative for obtaining registration. However, many Chinese consumers remain hesitant to adopt these alternatives due to insufficient charging infrastructure and high costs, leading some affluent residents to simply for owning a car altogether.

Baltimore police officials believe that recent rioting in the city was partly inspired by rumors spread on social media regarding a "purge," which refers to the fictional events in the popular horror movie franchise. The unrest, which began after the death of Freddie Gray in police custody, saw high school students allegedly organize attacks on a shopping mall and other locations. The chaos was fueled by online posts claiming a day of lawlessness similar to the dystopian premise of "The Purge" movies.

Tanka Maya Sitoula, a 40-year-old mother of four, survived 36 hours trapped in the rubble of a collapsed building in Kathmandu following Saturday's deadly 7.8-magnitude earthquake. She was finally freed by an Indian rescue team after enduring the ordeal without injury. Sitoula remained confident that she would be rescued throughout her time trapped, while her husband never stopped calling for help despite the lack of immediate equipment.

Miami International Airport police have deployed hidden cameras to investigate a significant insider threat problem involving baggage handlers who pilfer passengers' valuables. A CNN analysis reveals that Miami, New York's JFK, and Los Angeles airports top the list for luggage theft claims, resulting in $2.5 million in reported losses between 2010 and 2014.

C-SPAN’s live telecast of the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, hosted by Cecily Strong, was criticized for its lengthy duration and lackluster humor, though it featured some genuinely funny moments. President Barack Obama delivered a highly praised performance as the warm-up act, showcasing sharp comedic timing and clever jokes that outsh Strong’s more controversial material. Ultimately, the event was viewed as a testament to American tolerance and press freedoms, despite the challenging audience reaction to Strong’s set.

Lifetime has greenlit "The Unauthorized Full House Story," as a follow-up to its previously "Saved by the Bell" TV movie, which will explore the cast's rise to fame and the contrast between their idyllic on-screen lives and their complex real-world struggles. Casting for the project is set to begin immediately, though an air date has not yet been determined. The film, written by Ron McGee and produced by the same team behind the "Saved by the Bell" story, aims to replicate the success of its predecessor despite that previous film's modest viewers ratings.

Chile's Calbuco Volcano erupted on Thursday, marking its third event in a week, which authorities described as less severe than the previous two explosions. Approximately 1,500 people have been evacuated from the area, and a 2-kilometer exclusion zone has been established as ash spreads into neighboring Argentina.

Critics generally acclaim "Furious 7" as the best installment in the franchise, praising its high-octane action sequences and emotional tribute to the late Paul Walker. While some reviewers note that the plot and acting have typical franchise flaws, they agree that the film successfully balances spectacular stunts with a heartfelt sense of camar and loss. The consensus is that the movie honors Walker’s memory without letting his real-life death overshadow the fun and excitement of the film.

However, subsequent DNA tests proved that Alondra is not related to the woman, leading to her return to Mexico and leaving her biological family to fight for justice.

English actress Michelle Keegan has named the sexiest woman in the world by British men's magazine FHM. Keegan, known for her roles on "Coronation Street," tops the list alongside celebrities such as Kendall Jenner and Jennifer Lawrence. The magazine's "FHM 100 Sexiest Women in the World" issue hits stores on April 30.

Lilienstein, who moved to Canada in 1996, was a key member of the singing trio that launched in 1978 and became an icon in children's television across North America. Andrew Lesnie, the Academy Award-winning cinematographer known for his long collaboration with Peter Jackson on "The Lord of the Rings" and "The Hobbit" films, has died at the age of 59. Lesnie suffered a heart attack on Monday, and his family is expected to release an official statement regarding his passing. celebrated for his work on films such as "King Kong" and "Rise of the Planet of the Apes," Lesnie leaves behind a legacy of innovative visual storytelling and technical mastery.

Justin Timberlake and Jessica Biel have welcomed their first child, a son named Silas Randall Timberlake. The couple announced the birth via statements to People, revealing that the name honors both of Timberlake's maternal grandfather and his own father. This marks the first baby for both celebrities, who had previously announced the pregnancy in January.

Bahamian R&B singer Johnny Kemp, best known for his 1988 hit "Just Got Paid," died this week in Jamaica, where he was believed to have drowned at a beach in Montego Bay. The singer was scheduled to perform on a cruise but had not yet boarded the ship when the incident occurred. Tribers, including Chris Kirkpatrick and Samuel L. Jackson, have paid tribute to Kemp, who earned a Grammy nomination for his chart-topping single.

Major corporations and political figures across the spectrum are adopting "Ban the Box" policies, which remove criminal history questions on initial job applications, to leverage untapped labor market potential. These fair-chance hiring reforms aim to reduce recidivism and address systemic racial disparities by evaluating applicants based on their skills rather than past mistakes.

During Supreme Court oral arguments regarding marriage equality, Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg highlighted the historical evolution of marriage, noting that it was formerly defined as a dominant and subordinate relationship where women had limited legal rights.

 Attorney Mary Bonauto agreed, explaining that these gender-based legal distinctions have since been eliminated due to changing social circumstances and a push for equality. The article further contextualizes these arguments by referencing the history of anti-misceenation laws and Justice Clarence Thomas’s personal background, suggesting that the definition of marriage has consistently shifted over time.

The report describes a Kabul transformed by the legacy of America's longest war, where former Afghan interpreters who worked for NATO are now blacklisted, unemployed, and living in fear of reprisals. The city is swollen with displaced residents yet shunned by foreigners, leaving streets and businesses deserted as the physical remnants of the conflict gather dust.

Tennis legend Andy Murray married his long-term partner, Kim Sears, at Dunblane Cathedral in Scotland, which was dubbed "the royal wedding of Scotland" by the enthusiastic local crowd. Murray, who wore a traditional kilt, and his bride, who wore a vintage-style gown, were celebrated by residents who braved various weather conditions to witness the event. However, the couple's honeymoon plans have been postponed as Murray prepares to return to tournament action next week.

Photographer Simon Brann Thorpe created his project "Toy Soldiers" in the Western Sahara desert, featuring real soldiers posing as green plastic figurines to explore how the public consumes images of war. The project highlights the long-fought conflict between the Polisario Front and Morocco, which receives minimal mainstream media coverage. Thorpe used this visual metaphor to challenge viewers' desensitized responses to conflict imagery and provoke deeper emotional and political engagement with the ongoing crisis.

Percy Sledge, the soul singer who wrote and performed the classic hit "When a Man Loves a Woman," has died at the age of 73 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Sledge, who was undergoing hospice care for cancer, is best remembered for his 1966 No. 1 hit, which became a cornerstone of soul music and was later covered by artists such as Michael Bolton. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2005, leaving behind a legacy defined by his powerful vocal performances and enduring musical influence.

A Consumer Reports study analyzing 70 million passenger trips reveals that Southwest Airlines offers the highest availability of award tickets among major U.S. carriers, while JetBlue provides the lowest. The report advises consumers to carefully evaluate the value of their miles, noting that award tickets are not always the best financial choice, particularly for shorter, cheaper routes. Passers are encouraged to redeem miles on longer, more expensive flights to maximize the benefit of their loyalty points.

Gulnaz, a 16-year-old Afghan woman who was raped by her cousin's husband, was wrongly convicted of adultery and pardoned by the president, only to face intense societal pressure to marry her attacker. She is now raising her third child with him in a polymarous household. The case highlights the severe limitations on women's rights in Afghanistan, where conservative traditions often prioritize social "honor" over justice, forcing victims to accept abusive arrangements to avoid ostracization.

Freddie Gray died one week after his arrest in Baltimore, while police and his family’s attorney are disputing the circumstances of his injury and death. The incident has sparked protests and renewed national debates on race and policing, similar to the aftermath of Michael Brown’s death in Ferguson, as authorities conduct ongoing investigations into the officers involved.

A New York jury has been deliberating for ten days in the case of Pedro Hernandez, charged in the 1979 disappearance and murder of 6-year-old Etan Patz, but has yet to reach a unanimous verdict. Hernandez confessed to the crime three years ago, but his defense attorneys argue that his confession is unreliable due to his severe mental illness and borderline intellectual disability. The high-profile trial has kept the case in the public eye for over three decades, as Etan’s disappearance originally sparked a national era of heightened awareness regarding missing children.

Four rainbows appeared over New York after a heavy rain, captured by Amanda Curtis, whose photo quickly became a viral sensation on social media. Weather experts explained that the unusual sight was likely a double rainbow reflected in a body of water, a phenomenon that has previously captated the internet, such as the famous "double rainbow" video.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, announced plans to launch an unmanned rover to the moon by 2018, which would make the nation join the elite club of countries that have successfully landed craft on the lunar surface. The mission aims to perfect soft-landing technologies for future manned expedments to the moon and Mars. This move is seen as Japan's effort to compete with recent extraterrestrial successes by its Asian neighbors, China and India.

Baltimore mother Toya Graham became an internet hero after a video showing her slapping and pulling her son away from a violent protest was widely praised for her protective intervention. Graham stated she acted out of concern for her son's safety and embarrassment, after seeing him holding a brick during the unrest. The incident occurred as protests in Baltimore escalated into riots, prompting the city to impose a curcur. While some criticized the physical discipline, many online users celebrated Graham for prioriting her child's well over the escalating danger.

Five PKK militants and four Turkish soldiers were killed or wounded in clashes with Turkish armed forces in Agri, eastern Turkey. Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan strongly condemned the attack, which occurred ahead of a spring festival, while PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan continues to urge his followers to lay down their arms.

Federal researchers using an underwater drone have surveyed the wreck of the USS Independence, revealing images that show the aircraft carrier remains remarkably intact after 64 years on the sefloor. The ship, which survived a Japanese torpedo strike and two atomic bomb tests, was scuttled in 1951 near California's Farallon Islands. NOAA's survey highlights the vessel's historical significance as a "guinea pig" for nuclear testing and a key player in World War II.

A boat carrying nearly 950 migrants capsized in the Mediterranean, approximately 70 miles north of Libya, resulting in dozens of deaths and many others being trapped inside by smugglers who had locked the doors. Maltese Prime Minister Joseph Muscat condemned the human trafficians, labeling their actions as "genocide" for risking lives by using unsafe vessels. The Italian Coast Guard is currently leading the rescue operation and collecting statements from survivors to investigate the tragedy.

Prosperity gospel pastor Creflo Dollar has responded to critics who mocked his fundraising campaign for a $65 million Gulfstream G650 jet, by claiming that the "devil" is trying to discredit him. Dollar argued that the backlash is an attempt to stop him from spreading his message, while defending the need for the aircraft due to safety concerns with his older plane. The controversy originally erupted after Dollar solicited donations from hundreds of people globally to replace his 1984 Gulfstream, following two accidents involving the older aircraft.

The upcoming Mayweather vs. Pacquiao fight is likely to reinforce boxing's decline rather than save it, because the sport has been outpaced by the mixed martial arts phenomenon, the UFC. The author argues that our fascination with these bouts stems not just from bloodlust, but from a complex mix of civilized fascination and the guilty thrill of witnessing controlled violence.

At least 35 people, mostly child athletes, killed in a fiery bus collision with a fuel tanker in southern Morocco. The crash near Tan-Tan on Friday resulted in significant debris and smoke, with eyewitnesses reporting that the victims were traveling for a sporting competition.

Venezuelan citizen Marleni Olivo threw a mango at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, containing a written plea for help with housing, which the president publicly acknowledged by displaying the fruit. In response to her bold gesture, Maduro announced that he has approved Olivo’s request for a new apartment. The incident, which has gone viral, highlights Maduro's direct engagement with citizens' grievances, even amidst a polarized political climate where critics have mocked the event as a "mango assassination attempt."

Newly appointed Attorney General Loretta Lynch prioritizes a federal response to civil unrest in Baltimore, following the death of Freddie Gray in police custody, while her department investigates potential police misconduct. Lynch aims to balance community relations with legal accountability, utilizing tools such as withholding federal funds to address systemic issues within local police departments. The Justice Department has already launched probes into the Gray case and other recent incidents, signaling a firm stance on protecting civil rights and securing order amidst ongoing riots.

Ben Affleck successfully lobbied producers of "Finding Your Roots" to remove any mention of his ancestor owning slaves, which the show's host Henry Louis Gates Jr. ultimately did, despite later denying that the decision was based on Affleck's request. The controversy, revealed through hacked emails, has prompted PBS to launch an internal review to determine if the program violated its editorial standards.

A helicopter crash in Malaysia on Saturday that killed six people, including former US Ambassador Jamaluddin Jarjis and a senior aide to Prime Minister Najib Razak, has prompted an official investigation. The Malaysian prime minister has ordered an inquiry into the crash, which occurred near Kampung Pasir Baru, while authorities have recovered the flight recorder and expect to release a preliminary report within a week.

President Obama recently emphasized the public health risks associated with climate change, during a roundtable discussion and interview, highlighting how rising temperatures and extreme weather events are directly affecting human health. He encouraged citizens and healthcare professionals to pressure elected officials to take action, while also declaring a National Public Health Week to raise awareness about these issues.

The decision clears the path for the scheduled executions, as the court determined that granting clemency is a presidential prerogative rather than a matter for administrative litigation. Australia has repeatedly appealed for clemency and proposed a prisoner swap, but President Widodo has maintained a strict stance against granting amnesty to drug dealers.

Loeb claims the couple had previously agreed that any embryos could only be brought to term with both parties' consent, and he is seeking to void that agreement to proceed with implanting the embryos via a surrogate. This dispute highlights broader legal questions regarding parental rights and ownership of frozen embryos when couples separate without clear prior agreements.

Six survivors of the Paris kosher supermarket siege have sued French media outlet BFMTV for broadcasting their location during the hostage-taking, which they argue was dangerous live coverage. The lawsuit, which has triggered a preliminary investigation, accuses the outlet of endangering the hostages by revealing where they were hiding. BFMTV has apologized for the incident, stating that the information was mentioned only once based on police sources and was immediately retracted by the chief editor.

The Italian navy has retaken control of a fishing boat named Airone, which was seized by gunmen off the coast of Sicily, and arrested a Libyan soldier involved in the incident. The operation resulted in one fisherman being slightly injured by an accidental gunshot. This event highlights the increasing use of weapons by smugglers in the region, as they attempt to recover vessels used for transporting migrants to Europe.

The suspect, a former student who once worked for the victim, remains at large and is considered armed and dangerous. The investigation highlights a system where smugglers promise safety features like new motors and GPS, despite the high risk of death, as an estimated 1,000 migrants have already per trying to reach Europe this year.

Scientists from the University of Utah have discovered a massive new magma reservoir beneath Yellowstone National Park, which holds enough hot rock to fill the Grand Canyon nearly 14 times. The discovery provides a clearer understanding of the park's geothermal system and its history of massive prehistoric eruptions. However, researchers emphasize that the hazard of an imminent eruption remains extremely low, with the USGS estimating the annual probability at 1 in 700,000.

Netflix has officially announced a "Full House" reunion special followed by a new spinoff series titled "Fuller House," which will star Candace Cameron Bure as the recently widowed mother of three boys. The original cast members, including Jodie Sweetin and Andrea Barber, are confirmed to return, while talks with other co-stars are ongoing. The new series is scheduled to premiere next year, aiming to appeal to both original fans and a new generation of viewers.

Hungarian architect Matyas Gutai has developed a prototype house using "liquid engineering" that incorporates water between its structural layers to regulate indoor temperature and reduce energy consumption. The innovative design utilizes stored heat to reheat the building when temperatures drop, creating a sustainable system that can produce its own energy and lower carbon emissions. Gutai’s concept, inspired by the thermal properties of hot baths, redefines architectural permanence by prioriting adaptability over traditional solid construction methods.

The United States has deploying warships to the waters off Yemen to monitor Iranian vessels, which Washington officials stated creates "options" for how America could respond to Iran's alleged arms trafficking to Houthi rebels. The Obama administration maintains that the primary purpose of this military positioning is to ensure the safety of international shipping lanes and to reassure regional allies, rather than to directly intercept Iranian ships. While the move serves as a clear warning to Tehran regarding the transfer of weapons, U.S. officials emphasize that their immediate goal remains securing maritime security and freedom of navigation.

Amid ongoing Saudi airstrikes and intense ground fighting, the Yemeni city of Aden remains divided between Houthi rebels and forces loyal to President Hadi, resulting in widespread fear and desperation among civilians. The conflict has caused hundreds of deaths and severe shortages of basic necessities like food and electricity. Despite Saudi efforts to support loyalist forces, the Houthi fighters have retained significant control, leaving the city in a state of limis and ongoing violence.

Jerome R. Hunt, a 54-year-old man from California, was apprehended after climbing a White House fence on Sunday night carrying a suspicious package. The package was subsequently deemed harmless, and Hunt remains in custody with charges pending. This incident has renewed calls for improved security measures, following recent criticism of the Secret Service over previous breaches of the White House perimeter.

An Alaska Airlines flight from Seattle to Los Angeles was forced to return to the airport after the pilot heard unusual banging noises from the front cargo hold. Upon landing, authorities discovered a Menzies Aviation ramp agent who had fallen asleep during baggage loading; he was in good condition, passed a drug test, and was released. The plane subsequently departed for Los Angeles with all 170 passengers and six crew members on board.

Major League Baseball and the Baltimore Orioles announced that Wednesday's game against the Chicago White Sox will be played without fans in attendance, following the unrest in Baltimore. The closed-door contest aims to minimize safety concerns and follows the postpon of previous games, with tickets being exchanged for future dates. This decision marks a rare instance in MLB history, as the league stated it is unaware of any prior closed-door games.

The Wisconsin Badgers defeated the Kentucky Wildcats 71-64 to end their perfect season, and will face Duke in the NCAA men's basketball championship game. Duke secured their spot in the title match by dominating Michigan State with an 81-61 victory. The Badgers rallied from a late deficit to secure their first Final Four appearance since 1941, while Duke's offense, led by Justise Winslow and Jahlil Okafor, proved too strong for Michigan State to overcome.

Judge Jeffrey Sutton’s opinion upholding state bans on same-sex marriage is the only recent appellate court decision to support such restrictions, which has been the Supreme Court's consideration of whether gay and lesbian couples have a constitutional right to marry. The split in judicial rulings highlights the legal arguments states may use to defend their bans, despite widespread criticism that Sutton’s view is an outlier.

New Belgium Brewery and Ben & Jerry's are collaborating to create a salted caramel brownie ice cream-inspired beer, as both companies are B Corporations focused on social activism. The specific details of the campaign will be announced later this year, with the beer expected to hit shelves in the fall.

NASA's spacecraft MESSENGER will impact Mercury's surface on April 30 after running out of fuel, ending an successful mission that launched in 2004. The mission has significantly advanced our understanding of the planet, revealing key discoveries such as the presence of ice in Mercury's polar regions and capturing stunning images of the solar system's closest planet to the sun.

Saudi forces resumed airstrikes in southern Yemen on Wednesday, despite Houthi rebels' calls for peace talks to resume only after a complete halt of hostilities. This action followed the end of the initial "Operation Decisive Storm" and the start of a new initiative, "Operation Renewal of Hope," which was interrupted by a rebel attack on a government military brigade. The Houthis also released Yemen's Defense Minister, a move demanded by the United Nations earlier this month.

Xenophobic violence in South Africa has resulted in at least six deaths and widespread looting, prompting other African nations to evacuate their citizens from the country. The unrest, which erupted in Durban following controversial comments by Zulu King Goodwill Zwelithini, is driven by deep-seated resentment over unemployment, crime, and the perception that immigrants are taking local jobs. Despite President Jacob Zuma’s efforts to address these social concerns, the attacks continue to escalate, marking a disturbing recurrence of anti-immigrant violence in the nation.

North Charleston police officer Michael Slager has been charged in the murder shooting of unarmed Walter Scott, whose death was captured by raw video footage that contradicts Slager's claim of self-defense. The incident has triggered investigations by the FBI and the State Law Enforcement Division, as well as a probe into potential civil rights violations by the South Carolina attorney general. The case has drawn widespread attention for its clear visual evidence, which contrasts with the typical lack of accountability in police fatal shootings, and highlights broader statistical disparities in how police use deadly force against black individuals.

Sicily has become a major destination for thousands of migrants and refugees fleeing North Africa, leading to a significant influx of arrivals from Libya since last weekend. The current surge is driven by the lack of control in Libyan ports following the fall of Gadhafi, contrasting with previous periods when strong leadership restricted migration flows. This crisis follows the end of Italy's costly Mare Nostrum rescue program, which was replaced by a less funded EU operation, leaving the Mediterranean waters increasingly dangerous for those attempting the journey.

The attack, which occurred during a wave of unrest against foreign-owned businesses, resulted in Sithole’s death despite the efforts of Oatway and another journalist to rush him to the hospital. Amid a preliminary framework for a nuclear deal, Iranians and their government are expressing confidence and optimism, hoping for economic recovery and improved relations with the world. Baltimore officials and community leaders are debating the term "thug," used by President Obama and Mayor Stephanie Rawlings-Blake to describe rioters, whether it is an offensive racial dog-whistle or a valid description of criminal behavior. The controversy has sparked a broader discussion about how the word is perceived in the context of the unrest following Freddie Gray's death, with some arguing it serves as a modern substitute for racial slurs while others maintain it simply describes misguided youth who must be held accountable.

The article argues that Oz has successfully turned the tide of criticism, despite previous controversies involving Senate testimony and media scrutiny of his weight-loss claims. However, this resilience comes at a significant cost to Columbia University and New York Presbyterian Hospital, which continue to support him despite the ongoing ethical and scientific disputes surrounding his practices.

Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, a top leader of the terrorist group Lashkar-e-Taiba, has been released on bail in Pakistan after years of detention, sparking strong condemnation from India. Lakhvi was charged in 209 for his role in planning the deadly 2008 Mumbai terror attacks that killed over 160 people. While Pakistan’s government defended its counter-terrorism efforts, India accused Pakistan of maintaining a "dual policy" on dealing with terrorists who threaten India.

Suzanne Crough, the child actress who played Tracy Partridge on the 1970s sitcom "The Partridge Family," has died at the age of 52. She passed away Monday at her home in Laughlin, Nevada, according to the Clark County Coroner's Office. Crough, who appeared in the show from 170-74, later worked as an office manager and raised two daughters in Los Angeles.

The election of 72-year-old former general Muhammadu Buhari in Nigeria, replacing outgoing President Goodluck Jonathan, represents a historic, peaceful transition of power that signals a mateness in West African politics. Buhari’s victory on an anti-corruption platform reflects widespread public frustration with elite venality and economic instability. The article argues that this shift offers a crucial opportunity to dismantle the entrenched system of crony capitalism and address the deep-seated corruption that has long plagued the nation.

The manuscript, dated September 1983, reveals early character details such as Claire Standish being originally named Cathy Douglas. District officials plan to display the script as a significant piece of local film and history, noting the rare connection to the iconic movie filmed at their former high school.

"Monty Python and the Holy Grail," celebrates its 40th anniversary as a cult classic that was initially made with a low budget but ultimately became a massive box-office success. The film, a spoof of Arthurian legend, overcame production challenges to become a comedy staple, generating significant revenue and enduring cultural impact through its iconic dialogue. It is widely regarded as the most quintessential and quotable entry in the Python filmography, despite its loose plot structure.

During his recovery, Green earned his college degree and gradually returned to the court, emerging with a renewed appreciation for life and a mission to raise awareness about hidden heart risks.

The alert highlights the dangers of these substances, which are often marketed decept as legal plant materials but contain unpredictable and harmful chemicals. Health officials warn that these drugs can cause severe symptoms ranging from seizures to loss of consciousness, particularly affecting teens who may be misled by their packaging.

Comedian Amy Schumer stole the show at the 2015 TIME 100 gala by performing a staged fake fall on the red carpet, directly in front of Kanye West and Kim Kardashian. This stunt was part of a busy week for Schumer, which also included the premiere of her third season of "Inside Amy Schumer" and a memorable appearance on "The Late Show with David Letterman." Social media platforms were trending with discussions about Hillary Clinton's official campaign announcement, including hashtags like "#WhyImNotVotingforHillary." Swedish prosecutors previously refused to conduct the interview in Britain, arguing that Assange’s presence in Sweden was necessary for any potential trial, but now accepted the meeting to prevent the statute of limitations from expiring in August 2015. Assange, who has been granted political asylum by Ecuador since 2012, denies the charges and fears being extradited to the United States.

Researchers attribute this epidemic to a lack of outdoor sunlight exposure during childhood development rather than academic pressure or screen time. However, experts argue that increasing time spent outside is the most effective prevention, though cultural emphasis on rigorous schooling often makes implementing this solution difficult.

The article argues that this political stunt serves as a strategic move to bolster Clinton's populist image and address perceptions of her being out of touch with ordinary Americans. The scheme involves a female officer falsifying a passenger's gender to trigger a groin scan, allowing a male colleague to conduct an inappropriate pat-down. The TSA has condemned the actions as egregious, but noted that criminal charges are unlikely because no specific victims have been identified.

These 140-page guidelines were developed following a 2213 federal ruling that declared the "Stop, Question and Frisk" practice unconstitutional due to its disproportionate impact on African-American and Hispanic communities. The updated curriculum aims to align police conduct with current laws and policies, emphasizing respectful interactions to build community rapport.

Iranian President Hassan Rouhani and Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei have stated that any final nuclear agreement must be removed economic sanctions on the first day of implementation, while Khamenei expressed skepticism about the deal's finality due to past U.S. commitments. The preliminary agreement reached with six world powers allows negotiators until June 30 to finalize the terms, though the U.S. insists sanctions relief will occur in phases rather than immediately.

As ISIS militants advance on Ramadi, Falih Essawi, the deputy head of the Anbar Provincial Council, describes the collapsing security situation from the front lines. Essawi, who is armed and positioned on the front line, urgently calls for Iraqi government reinforcements and U.S.-led air support to save the city. The offensive has triggered a mass exodus, with at least 150,000 residents fleeing Ramadi as ISIS gains control of key areas.

Dozens of Americans, including Muna Mansour’s family, are trapped in Yemen due to ongoing airstrikes between Saudi Arabia and Houthi rebels, while the U.S. State Department deems direct evacuation too dangerous. Mansour, a New York resident, describes the dire conditions for those waiting at the port, where families are squeezed into cargo holds with little food or sleep. As other nations successfully evacuate their citizens, U.S. organizations have filed a lawsuit against the government over its refusal to conduct an evacuation operation.

New research from NASA's Curiosity rover suggests that salty water may exist in small quantities on Mars, during the nighttime hours, despite the extreme cold conditions. This finding supports the theory that brines—tiny pockets of liquid water— could persist in certain areas, potentially explaining geological features like channels formed by running water. While these conditions are still too harsh to support terrestrial life, the discovery strengthens the case for past habitability and guides future exploration efforts.

The Shanghai Auto Show focuses on vehicle models rather than "car babes," as global manufacturers compete in the world's largest car market to launch new vehicles tailored to Chinese preferences. The event highlights a shifting landscape where foreign brands face increasing competition from domestic rivals like Geely, who are gaining market share and beginning to export to developed regions. Despite slower growth, China remains the industry's most critical market, with SUVs emerging as a key segment for both local and international automakers.

Critics, including Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International, argue that the new decree effectively establishes a dictatorship by granting Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha unlimited authority to curb any activities deemed harmful to national stability. "The Late Show with David Letterman" announced star-studded guests for its final month, including Oprah Winfrey, Bill Murray, and George Clooney, ahead of the show's conclusion on May 20. Letterman, who has hosted the program for nearly two decades, will be succeeded by Stephen Colbert on September 8. The upcoming episodes will feature a mix of high-profile celebrities and former collaborators to celebrate the end of an era.

Three men were arrested in connection with the incident, with one remaining in custody on charges including obstructing governmental administration. The police are currently investigating the cause of the fight, which witnesses described as chaotic and comparable to a wrestling event.

A massive avalanche triggered by the earthquake in Nepal struck Everest Base Camp, resulting in at least 17 deaths and dozens of injuries, while the national death toll exceeds 3,300. The disaster has stranded hundreds of climbers on the mountain, as aftershocks have rendered the dangerous Khumbu Icefall impassable for descent. Helicopters have been conducting ongoing rescue operations to evacuate stranded climbers and Sherpas from higher camps to safety.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez was sentenced to life without parole for the 2013 murder of Odin Lloyd, who was a former semi-pro football player and Hernandez's friend. During the sentencing, Hernandez maintained his innocence, stating "I didn't do it," while Lloyd’s family offered forgiveness and remembered him as a loving son and protective brother. The court emphasized that Hernandez's status as a professional athlete meant nothing in the face of the jury's verdict, which held him accountable for what prosecutors described as a brutal and senseless killing.

The University of Florida and Emory University are investigating allegations that Zeta Beta Tau fraternity members disrespected wounded war veterans during a Panama City Beach retreat by spitting, urinating, and pouring beer on them. The fraternity has expelled three members from the University of Florida chapter and suspended activities at both schools, while issuing an apology for the "ugly and unacceptable behavior." Emory University stated that no evidence implicits its students in the incidents, which organizers say occurred while veterans were attending a Warrior Beach Retreat at the same resort.

After struggling to maintain her triathlon training schedule during a harsh Chicago winter, the author decided to "partner up" with friends to stay accountable. She organized group workouts for swimming, biking, and running, which provided the necessary motivation and support to help her successfully complete her first marathon and improve her overall fitness.

NASA's New Horizons spacecraft has transmitted its first color images of Pluto and its largest moon, Charon, after a nine-year journey through the solar system. The probe is approaching its closest flyby on July 14, where it will capture sharper images and data to reveal details about the dwarf planet, its moons, and the Kuiper Belt.

The author, recalling events from 1945, describes the sudden shock in the Chicago Daily News office when telegraph editor George Dodge received the news that President Franklin D. Roosevelt had died. The newsroom immediately erupted into chaotic activity as editors rushed to prepare emergency bulletins and coverage for the newspaper's final edition. Local officials in the U.S. Virgin Islands are investigating after a Delaware family fell gravely ill and two teenage boys remain in comas, linked to improper pesticide application at the Sirenusa resort. The deadly chemical, methyl bromide, was used illegally by pest control company Terminix at multiple locations, including the governor’s condominium complex. Authorities are currently tracking down vacationers who may have been exposed to the banned substance while the affected family members slowly recover.

Researchers successfully extracted DNA from the remains of "Altamura Man," an approximately 150,000-year-old Neanderthal whose skeleton was discovered in an Italian cave in 1993, making him the oldest Neanderthal to have his genetic material sequenced. The decision to leave the bones in situ was made to prevent damage, allowing scientists to extract a sample from the shoulder bone without risking the destruction of the calcite-covered remains. This breakthrough provides crucial insights into early Neanderthal life in Europe and the broader evolution of hominids.

While ISIS presents itself as a global threat, its strength actually stems from local Sunni grievances in Iraq and Syria. The author suggests that ISIS's brutal governance will likely lead to internal disen among the populations it controls, potentially undermining its long-term stability.

Pope Francis will make a stop in Cuba in September on his way to the United States, following his successful mediation efforts that restored diplomatic relations between Havana and Washington. The visit has been met with joy by many in Cuba, who view it as a positive step for the country. The Pope, who played a key role in negotiating the thaw in U-S-CU relations, will address the U.N and Congress during his broader U States tour later in the month.

Hillary Clinton officially declares her presidential candidacy, bringing a political dynasty that has nearly monopolized the White House for decades, but critics question what specific platform she actually represents. While Clinton has championed progressive economic policies, her close ties to corporate donors and controversial foreign policy decisions, such as her vote for the Iraq War, leave her vulnerable to challenges from the political left regarding her commitment to inequality and ethical standards.

A&E, Lifetime, and History Channel have announced a remake of the classic 1977 miniseries "Roots," which will simulcast in 2016 to reach a new generation of viewers. LeVar Burton, who starred in the original production, will serve as co-executive producer on the new adaptation. The updated series aims to bring the powerful story of Kunta Kinte’s struggle against slavery to contemporary audiences while consulting historians for added authenticity.

The article argues that the Baltimore riots are not merely a local problem but a national collective failure, which the author personifies as "we" by claiming both America's historical achievements and its systemic injustices. The author contends that citizens cannot disclaim responsibility for these events while claiming credit for the nation's successes. Furthermore, the piece criticizes how political polarization turns such tragedies into partisan arguments, preventing a unified approach to addressing the deep-rooted issues of racial inequity and police brutality.

Turkish archaeologists discovered a stone chest in a 1,350-year-old church that initially appeared containing a piece of Jesus' cross, but the mystery deepened when the box was later found to be empty. This incident highlights the ongoing controversy surrounding the authenticity of "True Cross" relics. The article traces the history of these relics from Saint Helena’s 4th-century discovery to modern scientific analysis, questioning whether surviving fragments are genuine or elaborate forgeries. Ultimately, the piece suggests that the existence of these relics remains a matter of divine faith rather than historical certainty.

The underwater search area for missing Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 will likely to be double in size, after teams covering 60% of the current priority zone have found no trace of the aircraft. The expanded search area, roughly the size of Pennsylvania, could take up to a year to complete. The current priority zone is expected to be finished by May, with officials aiming to cover all high probability areas to provide answers to the families of the 239 people on board.

Amidst the unrest in Baltimore following the death of Freddie Gray, local business owners like Amanda Rothschild of Charmington's chose to temporarily close their shops to show solidarity with the community and support peaceful protests. While some establishments, like Charmington's, provided free food and water to demonstrators, others suffered significant damage from the riots. The situation has since evolved into a more peaceful atmosphere, with businesses balancing the need for community support against the financial losses incurred by the violence.

DC Entertainment, Warner Bros. and Mattel announced a partnership to launch "DC Super Hero Girls," featuring iconic female superheroes as relatable teens aimed specifically at girls ages 6-12. The initiative has sparked mixed reactions, with some praising the representation while critics argue that segregating the products by gender reinforces harmful gender divides. The franchise, which includes toys, books, and TV specials, is scheduled to roll out starting this fall.

Five years after the Deepwater Horizon oil disaster, the author's recent visit to the Gulf Coast reveals that the region's recovery is incomplete, despite BP's claims that conditions have returned to normal. While significant cleanup efforts have been made, studies indicate millions of gallons of oil remain on the seafloor and many safety reforms have yet to be implemented. The article argues that despite some progress, the environmental and economic damage persists, necessing continued vigilance and action to prevent future tragedies.

Henry Louis Gates accused Ben Affleck of pressuring him to scrub a segment about slaveholding ancestor Benjamin Cole from his PBS documentary "Finding Your Roots," while Affleck admitted to feeling embarrassed by the discovery. The controversy intensified after leaked Sony emails revealed that network executive Michael Lynton advised Gates to remove the content to avoid potential sensitivity, despite Gates' denial that he violated editorial rules. critics argue that Gates missed a crucial opportunity to confront the legacy of slavery and racism, by prioriting "compelling television" over historical truth.

The arrest of North Charleston police officer Michael Slager for the shooting of unarmed Walter Scott has been justified by the exonerated video footage, which contradicted Slager’s claim that he feared for his life. The incident highlights the stark contrast between North Charleston’s handling of the case and the controversy surrounding the Ferguson shooting, particularly regarding racial disparities in police forces. the article argues that the video evidence in North Charleston allowed authorities to address the injustice more effectively than in Ferguson, where similar issues of racial bias and lack of transparency persisted.

Hillary Clinton’s campaign announcement video emphasizes the experiences of everyday women, while she personally appears only briefly, signaling a shift in her messaging strategy. Clinton is betting that the current political climate is favorable for a woman president, noting the increasing acceptance of feminism and the historic number of women in Congress. However, despite broad public support for the idea of a female leader, significant partisan divides remain regarding whether Americans are ready for Hillary Clinton specifically.

Ibrahim al-Rubaish, a top leader of al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) and a former Guantanamo Bay detainate, was killed in a U.S. airstrike in Yemen. The death highlights the group's vulnerability amidst the country's escalating civil war and political chaos. AQAP has recently exploited the instability, benefiting from prison breaks that freed senior members and the recent withdrawal of U.S. special operations forces.

Senator Elizabeth Warren insists she is not running for president, but her recent comments on the qualities she seeks in a 2016 candidate—specifically a champion for the middle class who will lower student loan interest rates and protect Social Security—strongly suggest she is positioning herself for a potential bid. While Warren declined to rule out a run, she explicitly disqualified Republican candidates Ted Cruz and Rand Paul based on their voting records, leaving the door open for her to enter the race once other contenders clarify their platforms.

The trial will examine the seven minutes following the initial 911 call, along with evidence suggesting Holmes premed the attack and set booby traps at his apartment. Jurors will also review events before and after the shooting, including Holmes' academic background and his refusal to accept a guilty plea deal that would have spared him from capital punishment.

SpaceX has rescheduled its Falcon 9 rocket launch for Tuesday, aiming to attempt the first-ever landing of a booster stage on an autonomous drone ship in the Atlantic Ocean. The mission will carry an uncrewed Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station to deliver supplies, including an espresso maker. If successful, this landing would significantly reduce the cost of space access by enabling rocket reuse, a goal that has eluded SpaceX in previous attempts.

A Syrian migrant recounts his desperate journey from Dubai to Turkey, after losing his job and having his visa expired, and ultimately to Europe via a dangerous sea crossing. He details the high costs, risks, and dehumanizing conditions of using human smuggers, emphasizing that the peril was worth enduring to escape the conflict in Syria and secure a better life.

During his annual Q&A session, Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed Western sanctions as merely aimed at constraining Russia's development and predicted they will not be lifted anytime soon. He also defended the sale of air defense systems to Iran, arguing that the weapons are for defense and that Iran poses no threat to Israel. The event, which drew millions of questions from the public, was criticized by opponents as a choreographed display of power rather than genuine democratic engagement.

The Centers for Disease Control confirmed that the listeria outbreak linked to Blue Bell Creameries products has been lurking in the company's facilities since 2020, resulting in three deaths and over ten illnesses across multiple states. The CDC connected cases from 2010 to 2015 through DNA analysis, suggesting the bacteria could present in the factories for years. Blue Bell recalled its entire product line after positive tests for listeria were found in multiple locations, acknowledging that the source of contamination remains unknown.
